A1.justification: Both readable, 10-page PDFs describe the same DOF-GS work. Neither contains an appendix; both end with references and cite separate supplementary material that is absent from the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, camera-model analyses and ablations, including PSNR/SSIM and memory measurements in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments, quantitative results in Tables 1–3 and qualitative demonstrations in Figures 4–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same differentiable DOF renderer, learnable camera parameters, In-Focus Localization Network and optimization objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same real and synthetic defocus datasets from Ma et al. and retain the same refocusing, aperture-control and all-in-focus reconstruction scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains NeRF, Mip-Splatting, Deblur-NeRF, DP-NeRF, PDRF, BAGS and Deblur-GS. Table 2 retains the same Mip-Splatting and BAGS comparisons at higher resolutions.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain identical, including 40,000 optimization iterations, COLMAP estimates for synthetic scenes, PSNR/SSIM metrics and evaluation at 600 × 400, 1200 × 800 and 2400 × 1600.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 retains the focal-distance validation, CoC/mask visualizations and aperture/focus-control analyses. Section 4.4 and Table 3 retain the same detail-enhancement and regularization ablations.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative figures are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports DOF-GS PSNR/SSIM of 24.12/0.7667 on real scenes and 29.39/0.8914 on synthetic scenes in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18 and their mathematical reasoning are identical, including the thin-lens approximation, CoC-based Gaussian convolution and loss definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about post-capture focus/aperture control, learning camera parameters from defocused images and recovering sharp scene details.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanation that the two-parameter camera model limits flexibility relative to per-pixel kernels, the difficulty recovering regions blurry in every view and the proposed future use of camera-pose optimization.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-website URL below the affiliations, providing a new access pointer. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the linked site's contents.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 31 references are identical, including positioning against defocus-modeling NeRF/3DGS methods and surface-splatting approaches.

P1.justification: The title-page text gains the project URL and an updated arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology, headings and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added colored website line slightly changes the title-page layout. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–3 retain their content and presentation; rendered pages 2–10 are identical.

improvement.justification: The project link offers a small navigation convenience, but the method, experimental evidence, explanations and limitations are unchanged. The supplied PDFs establish no new technical resources or evidence beyond that pointer, so the title-page update does not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
